\chapter{Writing --- Four Lines, And The Gap Inside A Word}
\label{ch:fa-four-lines}
\hlchaptermodality{289}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write four connected lines of Persian to a named reader, setting one thing against another with vali and giving a reason with chon.}

Complete FA-W289-chahar-khat: four lines to one reader, at least one with vali and one with chon, then check the spacing around every vav.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(four connected lines)]{Four lines, and the gap that sits inside a word}

\label{lesson:FA-W289-chahar-khat}



\begin{quote}
The last lesson asked for writing \textbf{finished on time}. This one asks for writing that \textbf{holds together}.

Pick one person who will read it: a friend, by name.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know — two joiners, one letter that will not join}
Connected writing is not \textbf{longer} writing. Four short lines can be connected; one long line can fail to be. What makes it connected is that a sentence stops standing on its own.

You hold two joiners. \textbf{\fa{ولی}} sets one thing against another. \textbf{\fa{چون}} gives the reason.

And both of them carry \textbf{\fa{و}}, the letter that takes the hand of the letter on its right and offers nothing to the left. So each word breaks open after it: \textbf{\fa{و}} then \textbf{\fa{لی}}, and \textbf{\fa{چو}} then \textbf{\fa{ن}}. A Persian word can have a gap inside it.

That makes your spacing part of the spelling. The gap \textbf{between} words has to be clearly wider than the break \textbf{inside} one. Make them equal and a reader cannot tell whether \textbf{\fa{ولی}} is one word or two.

\subsection*{Writing — connected composition}
Write \textbf{four lines} to the person you picked, right to left.

At least one line must use \textbf{\fa{ولی}}. At least one must use \textbf{\fa{چون}} to give a reason.

Use only words you already write. This lesson adds no vocabulary; the whole exercise is the joining, and a simpler familiar line is better than an invented one. This attempt is untimed.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cover your first line and read the second alone. Does it still make complete sense without the first? If it does, you wrote a \textbf{list}, like the form one lesson ago.

Then find every \textbf{\fa{و}} you wrote. Is the break after it smaller than the space between your words? It should be.

Four untimed lines close this writing rung. They are not the 30 to 40 word message of the full A1 paper, and they do not prove A1 attainment, readiness, or human validation.
\end{tcolorbox}
